newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end firmer on institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end firmer on institutional buying.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed a shade higher on Friday as local institutions joined foreign investors to expand their portfolios, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.86 points higher at 591.41.
"Local and foreign institutions dominated the market today, using current low prices to take long-term positions," said Shanil Perera of Lanka Securities.
"More foreign orders should get done next week provided shares can be souced at reasonable prices," he said.
Price gains led declines by 25 to 15. Turnover rose to 54.4 million rupees from 25.1 million on Thursday.
John Keells Holdings rose three rupees to 180, Commercial Bank three to 108 and National Development Bank one to 191.
Foreign sales exceeded purchases by 31.3 million rupees to 22.3 million on Friday but local institutional buying supported the market, brokers sid.
Among actively traded were Distilleries, John Keells Holdings, Merchant Bank, Pelwate Sugar, Tea Smallholder and United Motors.
